Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: This is an affinity-purification (pull-down) proteomics study aimed at identifying ligands for MGL. While it uses a 'case' (MGL-Fc) and 'control' (EDTA) to filter for specific binders, it is not a perturbation study (e.g., drug treatment or genetic knockout) but rather a molecular interaction assay. Therefore, it is mapped as un-classified.

base_candidates_ranked.reason: Data-dependent acquisition (top-10 mode) was used with a semi-quantitative approach based on unique peptide counts across replicates and controls.

modifier_candidates_ranked.reason: The experiment specifically targets O-glycopeptides (Tn antigen) using oxonium ion triggering (m/z 204.087) and specialized search engines (Byonic) for glycan databases.

workflow: LUMOS mass spectrometer was operated in data-dependent MS/MS (top-10 mode)
product ion trigger was set on the HexNAc oxonium ion at m/z 204.087
raw data were analyzed with MaxQuant 1.5.1.2 using the Andromeda search engine
submitted to Byonic version 2.13.2 using default settings
Variable modifications set were oxidation (Met) and 'N-glycan 309 mammalian no sodium' or 'O-glycan 78 mammalian' databases
differential: proteins that were either never found in the negative control experiment but were found in at least two of the MGL pull-downs or proteins that were identified in all three MGL pull-downs and identified a maximum of one time in the negative control samples
search_parameters: Modifications taken into account in the search were oxidation (M), acetylation (N-term), and HexNAc (ST) as variable and carbamidomethyl (C) as fixed
Trypsin was selected as the enzyme, allowing up to two miss cleavages

Ontology_ProcessingAndDifferential_promp.notes: The study uses a pull-down enrichment strategy (MGL-Fc) to identify ligands. While the primary goal was protein identification (protein level), the validation focused on site-specific O-glycopeptides (Tn antigen) using oxonium-triggered HCD/CID and Byonic search.
